rows.verified: Rabies is a viral infection of the central nervous system affecting humans and other mammals.
Rabies remains present in mammals in many parts of the world, particularly in parts of Asia and Africa.
Potential exposure commonly follows a bite or scratch from an infected mammal.
People exposed abroad should not wait until returning to the UK before seeking assessment and starting indicated vaccination.
After returning to the UK, a person should contact a GP to ensure any post-exposure course is completed.
Pre-exposure prophylaxis guidance applies to people with an increased risk of rabies exposure.
Prompt rabies post-exposure treatment using vaccine, with immunoglobulin when indicated, is highly effective when given correctly.
UKHSA provides a coordinated public-health procedure for agencies responding to a suspected human rabies case.
Rabies risk depends on country, animal species, exposure type, wound site, timing, vaccination history and access to treatment.
Rabies guidance is exposure-, traveller-, animal-, treatment- and timing-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA Lyme disease and tick prevention
rows.verified: Lyme disease is a bacterial infection transmitted to humans through bites from infected ticks.
Ixodes ricinus is the tick species of greatest concern for human health in the UK.
Ticks are commonly associated with woodland, grassland, moorland, scrub edges, parks and gardens where animal hosts are present.
Ticks can be active throughout the year, with activity varying by life stage and season.
People should check skin and clothing after outdoor activity and pay attention to folds, the hairline and other common attachment sites.

rows.source: UKHSA Lyme disease signs and symptoms
rows.verified: An attached tick should be removed promptly with fine-tipped tweezers or a tick-removal tool by pulling upward slowly and firmly.

rows.source: UKHSA Lyme disease signs and symptoms
rows.verified: A spreading erythema migrans rash after a tick bite is characteristic of Lyme disease and should receive clinical attention.

rows.source: UKHSA Lyme disease management and prevention
rows.verified: Prompt recognition and a full course of appropriate antibiotics usually resolves acute Lyme disease without further complications.

rows.source: UKHSA Lyme disease and tick prevention
rows.verified: Lyme risk depends on tick species, infection status, attachment duration, habitat, season, clothing, removal timing and individual factors.

rows.source: UKHSA Lyme disease management and prevention
rows.verified: Tick and Lyme evidence is habitat-, exposure-, symptom-, diagnostic- and person-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
